title: Stochastic rollback orchestrator with shadow synthesis and A/B calibration
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: We need a single, auditable rollback advisor that can operate across canary, A/B, and shadow lanes. Current rollbacks rely on per-lane heuristics and ad-hoc thresholds; this PR introduces a stochastic rollback orchestrator that synthesizes shadow outputs to compute counterfactual A/B deltas, produces an explainable risk score, and can either auto-shelve a rollout or surface a ranked remediation playbook for operators.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds rollback/orchestrator service that consumes telemetry from canary, AB and shadow lanes and produces deterministic recommendations (shelve, auto-backout, hold, manual-review).
- Introduces shadow synthesis: lightweight deterministic replays against a saved request sample to build counterfactual output distributions when direct A/B pairing is sparse.
- Calibration pipeline for A/B comparisons that normalizes for request distribution drift and token-length sensitivity.
- Policy DSL extension (rollout-policy v2) for stochastic thresholds, confidence bands, and escalation routes.
- Telemetry: new metrics (rollback.delta_quality_score, shadow.consistency_ratio, rollback.confidence_interval) and a tracing facet for per-request explainability.
- Console: rollout detail page shows risk timeline and recommended playbook with one-click shelf/auto-backout (feature toggled).

Why stochastic? Many regressions are noisy or intermittent. The orchestrator models the distribution of deltas rather than relying on single-metric point checks. This reduces false-positive rollbacks while retaining fast automated remediation when a real regression is detected.

Compatibility and safety: The auto-actions are gated by: (1) configured risk budget, (2) minimum sample size over rolling window, (3) shadow-consistency guard to ensure synthesis quality. By default the feature ships disabled for managed accounts; default behavior is advisory only.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core orchestrator service and API
- [x] Shadow synthesizer + counterfactual replay harness
- [x] Policy DSL extension and validation schema
- [x] Telemetry registration and dashboard panel
- [x] End-to-end tests (unit + sim smoke)
- [x] Console UI wiring (behind feature flag)
- [x] Playbook and runbook content

Testing notes: Simulated rollouts were run against synthetic traffic (epochal drifts + intermittent regressions) and validated that the orchestrator suggested auto-backout only when delta_quality_score exceeded the configured risk budget with >95% confidence. Local integration tests include a small synthetic shadow dataset to validate synthesis fidelity.

Backward compatibility: rollout-policy v1 is still supported. v2 opt-in via policy_version: 2.0. Migration scripts included (dry-run).

Operational runbook: Added docs in docs/runbooks/rollback-orchestrator.md describing escalation, manual-shelf, and rehydration from snapshots.

Related: ENG-4128 (stochastic-safety-gates), ENG-4199 (shadow-synthesis-harness), SUP-7821 (customer incident prompting advisory automation).

review_comments: Diego Ramos (reviewer): Nice design. Two concerns: (1) the shadow synthesizer may bias results for long-tail prompts — can you add a stratified sampling mode? (2) the policy schema v2 fields need validation against legacy v1 during migration.
Asha Menon (author): Addressed — added stratified_sampling option to synthesizer and migration dry-run that validates v1 -> v2 invariants. See commit d4e5f6a and scripts/migrate_policy_v1_to_v2.py

Marco Liu (reviewer): Requesting a clarification: what happens if the shadow_consistency_ratio drops below the minimum during an active canary? Would the orchestrator pause the auto-backout path? Add explicit tests for this guard.

Asha Menon (author): Added test in tests/e2e/sim_rollouts/test_stochastic_rollback.py to assert that auto-backout is suppressed when shadow_consistency_ratio < configured_minimum; orchestration falls back to advisory state and flags operator alert.
Priya Patel (reviewer): Approved — added two small nit comments about logging verbosity in the scheduler (fixed).
